title: Critical Thinking
permanentRoutine: Question → Claim → Evidence → Assumption → Alternative → Limitation → Conclusion → Revision

assessmentModel.weekly: open-book reasoning checks plus authentic argument/evidence artifacts
assessmentModel.correction: below 80% on objective/scored reasoning components requires targeted correction and parallel-form or revised evidence
assessmentModel.protectedBoundary: browser-local drafts and self-checks do not create transcript credit

privacySafety.disagreementRule: Evaluate claims, evidence, assumptions, reasoning and trade-offs rather than assigning motives or identity labels.

crossCurricularReuse.rule: Existing resources may support instruction but do not become runtime dependencies or transfer assessment authority into this elective.

weeks.title: Claims, Questions & Evidence
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can I tell the difference between a claim, a question, an observation, and evidence?

days.task: Retrieve a prior reasoning move or inspect a new example connected to Claims, Questions & Evidence. Separate what is directly present from what is inferred.
days.evidence: retrieval note and observation/inference split for Claims, Questions & Evidence

days.task: Study the core vocabulary, reasoning structures, and a worked model for Claims, Questions & Evidence. Identify why the model is strong and where it could fail.
days.evidence: annotated worked model with vocabulary used in context

days.task: Compare at least two claims, arguments, sources, interpretations, or decisions related to Claims, Questions & Evidence. Rank them using explicit criteria.
days.evidence: guided comparison with criteria and justification

days.task: Apply Claims, Questions & Evidence to a new scenario. Test the reasoning against evidence, alternatives, uncertainty, and counterexamples.
days.evidence: claim-evidence map and source annotation

days.task: Revise the week's work after critique or self-check. Defend the conclusion, name a limitation, and state what evidence would change your mind.
days.evidence: revised artifact, limitation statement, and short defense

weeks.vocabularyTarget: 5–9 reasoning terms taught through use, examples, retrieval, and transfer

masteryCheck.retake: targeted correction then parallel-form or revised evidence
